title: Idolaters to Be Put to Death

reflections.title: "The LORD Your God Is Testing You"

reflect.text: Sometimes people see amazing signs or hear powerful voices that sound very convincing. Yet supernatural wonders can appear even in the service of false teaching. Miracles by themselves do not prove that a teacher speaks the truth. God allows such encounters as a test of our loyalty. He wants to show whether we truly love Him with all our heart and soul. A sincere, deep love for the Lord gives us spiritual discernment to see through deceptive wonders.

God does not test us because He needs to learn about us. As F. B. Meyer explains, God tests us so that He may "reveal us to ourselves." When we discover our own frailty, we are prompted to seek His great strength and ask for His grace, which is His undeserved kindness. The Lord tests us not only through confusing voices and changing opinions in the world, but also through small, quiet opportunities of service and the way we manage ordinary money.

questions: When you hear popular ideas or impressive claims, how do you check if they match your love for God?
How does recognizing your personal weakness help you lean on God's grace?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, help us to love You with all our heart and soul. When misleading ideas or confusing voices arise, give us clear wisdom to stay faithful to You. Show us our weakness so we may always depend on Your grace. Amen.

D2.author: John Piper
D2.work: Signs and Wonders, Heresy, and Love for God

reflections.title: Upholding the Truth

reflect.text: In ancient Israel, performing a miraculous deed was never enough by itself to prove that a messenger came from God. Even if a sign came true, any wonder-worker who tried to lure the covenant people into worshiping other gods was guilty of serious rebellion. The law commanded capital punishment for anyone who enticed the community toward idolatry, so that evil would be purged from among them and the people would fear God.

In our day, false teachers who claim divine authority remain one of the greatest dangers facing the church under the new covenant. Because of this, believers are called to protect the truth and uphold apostolic orthodoxy, which is the reliable faith taught by Jesus' apostles. We must be alert against the twisting of Scripture. Rather than tolerating harmful heresy, we are called to stand firm and lovingly confront doctrinal errors whenever they arise.

questions: Why is it dangerous to accept a teaching just because a person seems gifted or impressive?
How can we speak up against false ideas about the Bible while still showing love to others?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, keep Your church safe from teachings that twist Your Word. Give us courage to uphold the truth taught by the apostles and help us to speak against error with patience and love. Guard our hearts so we may always stay loyal to You. Amen.
